articles.title: Startups don't need to go viral to win customers | TechCrunch
articles.summary: At TechCrunch Disrupt last week, two founders and a VC discussed how to not just gain an early following but keep one.
articles.body_text: Getting initial customers as a startup can be one of the most grueling challenges in business. Even when companies manage to snag some early interest, there’s no guarantee those customers will stick around. At TechCrunch Disrupt last week, Elia Wallen, founder and CEO of travel startup Engine, Gamma founder and CEO Grant Lee, and Crystal Huang, general partner at Google Ventures, shared tips on how to attract and retain customers. In the current era — when young AI companies like Cluely and Instinct are building big audiences not just through their products but also through their founders’ colorful online presences — social media can seem like a magic bullet for reaching early customers. But founders who want heighten their business strategy with modern marketing, have to be strategic, according to Lee. Gamma, which sells AI-powered presentation software, managed to scale its business exponentially with a social media strategy that deployed influencers through its Ambassadors (or “Gambassador”) program. The company adopted the plan before influencer-based marketing was a tried-and-true strategy for smaller companies, eventually reaching a multi-billion dollar valuation . But simply giving influencers a platform and telling them to promote your brand online doesn’t automatically translate to sales, said Lee. There’s more to it than that. “If you have a product that can serve many different segments or use cases, then you want to basically have creators that can target each one of those,” Lee said. “If you have folks that are in consulting versus people that do all their marketing and create all the decks for their CMO, there’s all these different segments you might want to go after.” Lee said sometimes founders seem to treat creator marketing or influencer marketing as a sort of set it and forget it thing. “I think you’re better served by really spending a lot of time with these creators, because if they’re not able to understand how to articulate the value of your product, it doesn’t matter how much money you spend, it’s just going to fall flat,” Lee added. The effectiveness of social media depends largely on the type of business. Other ways of reaching customers can be just (if not more) effective. Wallen would know. His company Engine, which manages lodging and travel bookings for midsize businesses, bootstrapped its way to $150 million in bookings before taking on any outside funding. They also had no visible social media strategy at all. For Wallen, traditional sales tactics can be far more useful than a positive TikTok video. “We did events and we smiled and dialed,” said Wallen. “We still have a lot of people picking up the phone. A lot of people who didn’t grow up with that or don’t understand it think that it’s outdated or it doesn’t work but it does. It’s a hard thing. There are a lot of companies that just refuse to do it or don’t know how to do it well. But they’re missing out on a very big offline client base.” He added: “The phone still works.” Wallen also shared an in-person tactic that his company deployed during its scrappy early days: hiring a magician named David to perform tricks for prospective clients at events and encourage them to visit the Engine’s booth. In short, old-fashioned personal engagement can work just as well, if not better, than the latest social media tricks.

articles.title: OpenAI says it will no longer train its AI models on the live internet, citing “significant risks” | TechCrunch
articles.summary: OpenAI will cut frontier models off from the internet weeks after one of its engineers said that solution wouldn't work.
articles.body_text: On Friday, OpenAI said that it will train its models using cached copies and simulated versions of the internet instead of the live web because the models are too unpredictable to be trusted with live internet access. The frontier lab announced its new policy two weeks after its rival, Anthropic, began limiting its newest and, in theory, most capable models from accessing the live internet. Researchers adopted these policies after months of incidents in which models pursuing training tasks broke into external systems in search of answers, collaborated on obscure message boards, and developed exotic hacking strategies. “Based on the current state of alignment research, monitoring systems, and the security of internet infrastructure, we believe the responsible approach is to conduct frontier model training with no internet access,” the company said in a blog post . OpenAI said that as recently as September 20, one of its frontier models exploited a misconfiguration to access the internet. That led the company to pause training work for the rest of the month so it could develop and test new approaches to securing its models. The decision to train these models in sandboxes cut off from the internet is notable because employees at frontier labs have insisted that doing so would be nearly infeasible. Keeping AI data centers separate from the internet “would need research teams to essentially be embedded inside of data centers in Iowa or wherever else around the world,” former OpenAI researcher Steven Adler told Fortune this month. “It’s a lot of overhead, and it isn’t clear to me that the safety benefits of it are large enough to merit just how large a tax it would be for a company to do it unilaterally.” “In nearly every post I make on X, without fail, I get between five and ten comments about my inability to secure a sandbox, or asking why the hell we can’t just unplug the model from the internet,” an anonymous security engineer at OpenAI wrote in a September post on X. “These comments reflect a widening gap between where a lot of organizations and people are today and what the frontier labs are dealing with. There is also a general misunderstanding of how model training and evaluation work at these labs.” The engineer, whose role has been confirmed previously by OpenAI, described how complex the training runs launched by OpenAI engineers are, noting that they require access a variety of resources and tools across many domains, and that thousands of researchers build, modify and test the environments. “So is it as easy as just putting it in a sandbox? No, it’s not,” he concluded. Now, OpenAI says that “we must always be able to prevent a frontier model from achieving unauthorized, arbitrary access to the live internet.” That comes after the company deployed swarms of agents in red-teaming exercises that attempted to escape from their sandbox. That effort revealed a range of vulnerabilities that convinced the lab to adopt its new approach. To meet that requirement while still reaching its training goals, the lab said it created a “a vast set of indexed and cached web content with which our models can interact, without risk of affecting external systems.” Whether that strategy will perform as well as letting models run freely on the open internet remains to be seen, but it is noteworthy that both frontier labs have determined their most powerful technology can’t be left unsupervised on the digital commons. articles.body_text: Earlier this week, a video of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang playing with a flock of waddling Microducks during his keynote at the company’s GTC Berlin conference went viral. The robots, stomping their little feet and making tiny R2-D2 noises, sat, fell down dead for a “nap,” and summersaulted on voice command. articles.title: VCs, Superhuman Mail founder share red flags about product-market fit | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Top investors from Iconiq and Sapphire Ventures, along with Rahul Vohra, the founder of Superhuman Mail, share the do's and don'ts for building hit products.
articles.body_text: Product-market fit — when a startup’s product sells well — has become even harder to find in this AI era. Despite startups achieving record-fast growth, not all customers are sticky and products can be replicated more easily than ever. Anu Bharadwaj, a partner at Iconiq; Rajeev Dham, a partner at Sapphire Ventures; and Rahul Vohra, the founder of Superhuman Mail, discussed the new rules for product-market fit last week at TechCrunch Disrupt . “It’s never been easier to gain a bunch of pilots because lots of companies across the board are open to trying new things,” Bharadwaj said to the audience. “But going from pilot to production is really the hard thing.” Right now, she said, a lot of founders pitch revenue metrics to investors without specifying which revenue they are talking about. “Is it true ARR or is it run rate?” she said. “There’s many ways to obfuscate the whole thing.” Lately, much chatter on X has focused on AI founders inflating ARR numbers (which could mean “annualized run rate” or the more solid “annual recurring revenue”) to make it seem like their companies are doing better than they are. A common gimmick is counting pilot customers, who might only use the product for a couple of months, in the annualized run rate revenue number, implying that income is expected to continue for the entire year. It should be obvious, but Bharadwaj pointed out, “It’s definitely in your long-term interest that you be very honest and upfront about what quality of revenue this is.” She said companies need to separate hype from reality when looking at the quality of their revenue. It’s a red flag, for example, if only a few customers make up much of a company’s revenue or if the customers can easily go to another vendor for a better price. “Churn rate and retention [are] really dependent on that,” she continued. That’s why Vohra advises startups to track customer engagement and dollar retention, especially for consumer products. “Figure out what benchmark [is] good, great, and excellent for your space,” he said. For example, at Superhuman, he said that the company tracked ARR but also had their own internal metric called “delighted ARR,” which, he said, “was the ARR only from customers who are super engaged with the product.” He said that metric helped them see how sticky the customers were and how long they were likely to stay around. “Those users are now still users, those companies are now still customers,” he continued. “We obsessed over serving that particular category of our user base and our customer base.” The panelists also discussed green flags that indicate a startup has indeed found product-market fit. For Vohra, he said talk to customers to understand what value they find in the product and how they would feel if they could no longer use it. Then be honest with yourself when measuring those responses. “If you’re 15%, 14%, 13%, or below, consider a complete pivot. Take the codebase, take the team, build something entirely new. “But if you’re 20%, you can totally optimize your way from 20% to 40%,” Vohra said.

articles.title: Carta and NewView partner, hoping to entice more startups to let employees sell shares early | TechCrunch
articles.summary: A new program wants to encourage more startups to allow workers to cash out early by making it easier to transact tender offers.
articles.body_text: Startups are staying private longer, leaving employees, who typically take a portion of their compensation as stock they can’t sell, with little hope of early liquidity. An increasing number of late-stage startups are recognizing this and offering tender offers to employees. These are transactions that allow employees (and, often, early investors) to sell a portion of their shares for a predetermined price to an approved investor. To simplify the tender process, NewView Capital recently partnered with Carta. The collaboration combines NewView’s secondary deal-structuring experience with Carta’s equity platform. Ravi Viswanathan, founder and managing partner of NewView, pitches this as a way to help startups launch and manage liquidity programs more seamlessly. “The hope is that this partnership will make it easier for CEOs and companies to think about tenders,” he said. He wants founders to think about giving employees early liquidity as a “win-win-win” for workers, companies, and investors alike. A growing number of startups seem to agree. Over the past three years, tender offers increased threefold for Series C and later-stage startups, according to a recent study from NewView and Carta. Plus, the startups that do choose tender offers are no longer just the most valuable private companies, like OpenAI, Databricks, or Anduril, according to Viswanathan. For instance, last year, his firm, which specializes in secondary deals along with typical venture investments, helped facilitate a tender for Hightouch at a $1.3 billion valuation, when the marketing customization startup was seven years old. However, Carta and NewView also found that the overall share of startups launching these offerings remains relatively small, with just 44 executed in the first half of 2026. So Viswanathan wants to encourage other startups to consider tender offers, calling them excellent retention tools and morale boosters. A decade ago, being a unicorn was enough to attract talent, Viswanathan said, but with so many billion-dollar companies around today, that status may not be as much of a draw now. Offering a tender, he said, “is an opportunity to say you will also get liquidity in your journey with us.” Some of the companies that recently held tender offers include AI customer support startup Decagon , self-driving tech developer Wayve , and AI voice generator ElevenLabs , which executed two such offerings in less than a year. “The companies are staying private for 12 to 15 years. That’s not changing,” Viswanathan said. “In that interim, so that we don’t have this talent drain from high-quality venture-backed companies into their public counterparts, we need to make sure that there is liquidity for the employees.” When you purchase through links in our articles, we may earn a small commission . articles.title: Agent cloud startup Daytona hits $1B valuation backed by FirstMark and a who’s who of angels | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Daytona is building a cloud for agents that's like giving every agent its own computer. It has attracted founders of Stripe, Perplextity, Datadog, Mercor, and others as angels, it says.
articles.body_text: Daytona Platforms announced on Friday that it had raised a $60 million Series B round at a $1 billion valuation led by FirstMark Growth. The company says it has now raised a total of $91 million. The New York-based startup has attracted not just FirstMark (which also led its $24 million Series A in February), but also a host of well-known angels in this latest round. Daytona says they include Stripe’s Patrick Collison, Shopify’s Tobi Lütke, Perplexity’s Aravind Srinivas, Zoom’s Eric Yuan, Datadog’s Olivier Pomel, Quora’s Adam D’Angelo (who is also an OpenAI board member), and Mercor’s Brendan Foody. It also names Qualcomm Ventures, Samsung Next, and Okta Ventures as participants. Three-year-old Daytona is building a cloud specifically for long-running agents, which have different infrastructure needs than yesteryear’s software, the startup contends. “Agents don’t work like the long-lived services today’s cloud was designed for. They spin up thousands of short, stateful jobs nobody planned in advance, and they need a cloud built for that,” founder Ivan Burazin wrote in a blog post announcing the new round . Daytona’s cloud, he said, is like giving every agent its own computer, where agents have access to sandboxed versions of Linux, Windows, macOS, and GPUs, among other services, on the one platform. articles.title: Commonwealth Fusion Systems gets $85M to build better fusion-ready semiconductors | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Top-funded fusion startup Commonwealth Fusion Systems received an $85 million award from the federal government to advance conductors for fusion power plants.
articles.body_text: Commonwealth Fusion Systems (CFS) announced on Thursday that it would receive $85 million from the U.S. government to develop advanced chips for the fusion power industry. Fusion power startups have been racing to complete their first demonstration devices, with CFS aiming to turn on its Sparc reactor sometime next year. But building one reactor is just a proof point. If fusion startups want to build dozens of commercial power plants, they’ll need more durable power electronics and a robust supply chain. The new CHIPS Act award from the Department of Commerce, which also grants the government a stake in CFS, will help boost R&D and manufacturing capacity for semiconductors in the U.S., the company said. “Ultimately, that means a more capable, economical power plant and a stronger U.S. supply chain to build it,” Brandon Sorbom, co-founder and chief science officer at CFS, wrote in a blog post . CFS’s award will go toward supporting five different initiatives. The first is the advancement of silicon carbide power electronics. The semiconductors are widely used to manage high voltages, and they’re found in everything from LEDs and EVs to cell phone base stations and data centers. It’s also used in fusion machines, where intense bursts of electricity are used to drive the superconducting magnets that confine plasma inside a reactor. CFS will also use the award to develop next-generation radio-frequency power generators, which the company uses to heat fusion fuel, and advanced electronics that will enable faster control of the reactor and be hardened against radiation. The latter could help extend the lifespan of electronics within a fusion power plant, reducing operating costs. Lastly, CFS plans to use part of the CHIPS award to adapt AI hardware like GPUs and TPUs for power plants. “The funding would help improve the U.S. chip and power electronics industries at the same time it accelerates fusion energy’s progress toward the electrical grid,” Sorbom said. articles.title: What some of Anthropic’s backers are worth before its IPO | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Early-stage and follow-on investors in the AI lab are already sitting on major paper returns.
articles.body_text: Anthropic’s public listing, which is expected this year at a valuation of as much as $2 trillion, is bound to be a windfall for both early-stage and later-stage investors. But even at the company’s latest private market valuation of $965 billion, the stakes held by many of those VCs and early backers already total billions. Coatue , which first backed Anthropic in 2025 at a $183 billion valuation and co-led the AI lab’s last two funding rounds, has poured a total of $4.75 billion into the company. That stake, based on the last round’s price, is now worth roughly $7.5 billion, according to a person familiar with the matter. Coatue declined to comment. Below is what some other backers of Anthropic are worth based on the last round’s price, according to Bloomberg : Eric Schmidt: The former Google CEO invested in Anthropic’s Series A in 2021, when the startup was valued at $461 million, according to PitchBook data. Today, Schmidt owns about 1% of the company, and even at its current private valuation, his stake is worth nearly $10 billion. Iconiq: The investment outfit wrote a $6 billion check to Anthropic last year when the company was already valued at $183 billion. That massive late-stage bet is now worth $17 billion and has the potential to double at the IPO. Menlo Ventures: The VC firm led Anthropic’s Series D and has invested more than $1 billion in the company over time, a stake now worth $14 billion. Sequoia: The famed VC firm backed the AI lab for the first time only earlier this year, when the company was already valued at $380 billion. The $3 billion investment gave it about 1% ownership, which means it has already more than doubled its investment. Sound Ventures: The firm, launched by Guy Oseary and actor Ashton Kutcher, invested $35 million in Anthropic’s 2023 Series C round and has since funneled an additional $400 million into the company, resulting in a stake that’s worth billions now. (Kutcher left Sound Ventures this year to launch a new VC firm .) Spark Capital: The only VC firm known to hold a board seat at Anthropic invested $75 million in that same 2023 Series C round, when it was valued at $5 billion. articles.title: Trumps utbrott om ”vidriga” reklamen
articles.summary: Donald Trump rycker ut till ilsket försvar av reklamfilmen med skräckmamman Donna Arthur. I en aggressiv ordväxling slår han undan frågorna om sexuella övergrepp. – Det är en smart kvinna, säger han.
articles.body_text: Donald Trump rycker ut till ilsket försvar av reklamfilmen med skräckmamman Donna Arthur. I en aggressiv ordväxling slår han undan frågorna om sexuella övergrepp. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Hon tog mannen som misstänktes för våldtäkt på hennes dotter i försvar. Hon flydde rättvisan tillsammans med honom – och de förblev gifta till hans död 26 år senare. Hon blev av med vårdnaden om sina barn på grund av övergreppen och har inte träffat dem sedan 1978. Hon är dömd för djurplågeri och bedrägeri. Men trots hård kritik, både från politiska motståndare och partikamrater, fortsätter Donald Trump att försvara – och hylla – reklamfilmen där skräckmamman Donna Arthur avråder väljarna från att rösta på sin dotter, Amy Acton, som guvernör i Ohio. – Hon är en mamma, en smart kvinna, som säger att hennes dotter är en lögnare, säger han i en hetsig ordväxling med NBC News -reportern Monica Alba. Alba undrar om presidenten inte alls bryr sig om anklagelser om sexuella övergrepp. Presidenten svarar med ett utbrott. – Det här var ju en härlig person, eller hur? Du är en hemsk liten reporter, inte sant? Om min mamma hade sagt dåliga saker om mig, tror du då att demokraterna skulle ha spridit det? Men min mamma tyckte att jag var fantastisk. Trump slår också fast att han önskar att han hade haft lika bra reklamfilmer som den Actons motståndare Vivek Ramaswamy nu använder sig av. – Hennes mamma trädde fram i tv och sa att hennes dotter är en lögnare och en dålig person. Varför skulle man då inte lyssna på en mamma som säger så? Varför skulle ni inte göra det, fröken NBC?

articles.body_text: Larmet om branden i Hitlers historiska Kehlsteinhaus i de bayerska alperna kom strax efter 21 på fredagskvällen. – Kehlsteinhaus är helt övertänt, säger polisens talesperson. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Bilder visar hur enorma lågor slår ut från Örnnästet, Kehlsteinhaus, ovanför Berchtesgaden i det sydtyska förbundslandet Bayern. Man misstänker mordbrand, säger polisens talesperson till Bild . Enligt polisen har en person på motorcykel gripits i närheten av platsen. Enligt tidig information var Örnnästet tomt när branden bröt ut och det finns inga rapporter om skadade personer. Om byggnaden kan räddas är fortfarande under natten oklart. Kehlsteinhaus är en av Tysklands mest lända historiska platser och uppfördes av Martin Bormann, en av Adolf Hitlers närmaste, i slutet av 1930-talet och skänktes till diktatorn i 50-årspresent 1939. articles.body_text: Ytterligare en pojke häktas misstänkt för inblandning i mordet på Saba Abraham, 24, i Älvsjö. Dessutom har en 14-årig flicka anhållits. – Konkret vad medhjälpen har bestått i vill jag inte uttala mig om, säger åklagare Lukas Tigerstrand. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. För en vecka sedan sköts 24-åriga Saba Abraham till döds inne i Kämpetorpshallarna i Älvsjö. Hon jobbade på fritidsgården i Älvsjö och var i hallen på en aktivitet för unga. Sedan tidigare sitter två tonårspojkar häktade på sannolika skäl misstänkta för bland annat mord och i veckan greps ytterligare två pojkar. På fredagen häktades dem. Den ena pojken är däremot inte misstänkt för inblandning i själva Älvsjömordet. Den andra häktades på sannolika skäl misstänkt för medhjälp till mordet på Saba Abraham. Åklagare Lukas Tigerstrand vill inte berätta vem som givit honom uppdraget eller hur uppdraget sett ut. – Jag kan inte kommentera något av det nu, givet läget. Även en 14-årig flicka har under dagen anhållits. – Rubriceringen är medhjälp till mordet i Älvsjö. Men mer konkret vad medhjälpen har bestått i vill jag inte uttala mig om. Totalt är alltså fem personer misstänkta i utredningen. Tror du att det kommer bli fler gripanden?

articles.title: ”Ozempic face” – skönhetsjättarnas nya guldgruva
articles.summary: Utmärglat, åldrat och smått ihåligt utseende. Det är tecken på det nya fenomenet ”Ozempic face”. Nu arbetar flera skönhetsjättar för att hitta behandlingar mot fenomenet.
articles.body_text: Utmärglat, åldrat och smått ihåligt utseende. Det är tecken på det nya fenomenet ”Ozempic face”. Nu arbetar flera skönhetsjättar för att hitta behandlingar mot fenomenet. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. De flesta som tar läkemedel som Ozempic eller Wegovy går snabbt ner i vikt. Något som ofta medför slapp och hängig hud. En del får också ett utmärglat, åldrat och ihåligt utseende när deras ansikten tappar fett. Något som fått namnet ”Ozempic Face” . Nu arbetar bolag som L'Oreal, Galderma och Natura med att skapa produkter som ska motverka hudeffekterna av fetmaläkemedlen. Det handlar både om kosttillskott, krämer och olika sorters fillers, skriver Reuters. – Vi testar nu produkter på GLP-1-användare [GLP-1 är samlingsnamnet för medicin som sänker blodsockret och påverkar aptit och mättnadskänsla reds. anm] i separata studier, eftersom denna grupp konsumenter representerar ett betydande antal människor över hela världen”, säger Delphine Viguier-Hovasse, L'Oreals innovations- och prospekteringschef. Försäljningen ökar hela tiden och till 2030 uppskattar läkemedelsbolaget Pfizer att marknaden för fetmaläkemedel kan nå 150 miljarder dollar i årlig försäljning, skriver Reuters. Det motsvarar runt 1 486 000 000 000 kronor. Det är nästan lika mycket som hela svenska statens utgifter varje år. Expertkåren är dock splittrad kring om bieffekten ”Ozempic face” går att justera med krämer. Vissa menar att det kommer att finnas behandlingar som förbättrar utseendet och kvaliteten på den drabbade huden, men som inte åtgärdar volymtappet i ansiktet, rapporterar Reuters. Och oavsett, försäljningen av hudvårdsbehandlingar och även skönhetsingrepp för att behandla ” Ozempic face” ser ut att rusa. Enligt uppskattningar från konsultbolaget Boston Consulting Group kommer intäkterna för dessa behandlingar öka från 700 miljoner dollar 2025 till över 2 miljarder dollar 2030. articles.title: Flera ungdomar skadade i garagebrand
articles.summary: Minst sju ungdomar har skadats i en garagebrand utanför Borås. Branden startade av någon form av brandfarlig vätska.
articles.body_text: Minst sju ungdomar har skadats i en garagebrand utanför Borås. Branden startade av någon form av brandfarlig vätska. – Det är ett gäng ungdomar som har meckat i garaget, säger Viktor Fritzson, yttre befäl och räddningsledare. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Flera ungdomar har skadats efter att en brand uppstått i ett garage i Fristad utanför Borås . Enligt DN är barnen i 13-14-årsåldern. – Vi larmades till ett garage i Fristad efter en brand som hade uppstått av någon form av brandfarlig vätska, säger räddningstjänstens ledningsoperatör. Räddningstjänsten larmades till platsen 18.49. Tio minuter senare uppgav de att branden var släckt. Varför det har börjat brinna är oklart. När polisen kom till platsen var flera ungdomar där. Sju personer har skadats och flera är allvarligt skadade. Enligt GP är alla barn under 15 år. DN rapporterar att sex av de sju vårdas på intensivvårdsavdelningar. – Fokus var att få i väg samtliga till sjukhus för vård. När vi kom till platsen fick vi veta att folk redan lämnat med ambulans eller på egen hand, säger Tamara Fuentes, presstalesperson på polisen i Väst. Räddningstjänstens yttre befäl, Viktor Fritzson, uppger för Borås Tidning att flera ungdomar befann sig i garaget när branden startade. – Det är ett gäng ungdomar som har meckat i garaget och en liten mängd bensin har läckt ut och det har antänt, säger han. En granne säger till BT att det var stökigt på platsen. Hon hörde höga skrik från garaget.

articles.body_text: Riksdagsledamoten Mohamed Ali (V) ”hör inte hemma” i Sverige, skriver SD i ett utspel på X. Partiets presschef i EU tycker att han har agerat ”osvenskt”. Vänsterpartiet kallar inlägget för ”oacceptabelt och djupt beklagligt”. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Det är kontot SD i Europaparlamentet som på X har delat en bild där partiet skriver: Man uppmanar sen dem som håller med att kommentera med ett hjärta. Intill texten har man också lagt en pirathatt. När Expressen frågar Sverigedemokraterna vad de menar svarar Richard Byfält, presschef för SD:s delegation i EU-parlamentet. ”Uttrycket 'hör inte hemma' betyder att någon, eller något, inte 'har sin naturliga plats' eller 'sitt ursprung' i Sverige” , skriver han i en kommentar. Han påstår bland annat att Mohamed Ali fick medborgarskap ”efter att han uppgett felaktiga uppgifter till Migrationsverket”. Expressen har rapporterat bland annat om Mohamed Alis skulder och bolag, men inte hittat belägg för att han ska ha ljugit i sin ansökan om medborgarskap till Migrationsverket. Dock har uppgifter som han lämnat i medborgarskapsprocessen – om skulderna och bolagen – väckt frågor om sanningshalten som han ännu inte har besvarat, trots upprepade förfrågningar från Expressen . Utöver detta pågår en utredning om valfusk, som kopplas till Vänsterpartiet i Borlänge. Där är tre personer misstänkta men Mohamed Ali är inte en av dem.

articles.title: Rysslands svar om Melanias vapenvila
articles.summary: Nu bekräftar Ryssland och Ukraina att de är överens om en vapenvila, för att invånare ska kunna evakueras och förnödenheter föras dit. – Utan min insats skulle det vara omöjligt, säger presidentfrun Melania Trump.
articles.body_text: Nu bekräftar Ryssland och Ukraina att de är överens om en vapenvila, för att invånare ska kunna evakueras och förnödenheter föras dit. – Utan min insats skulle det vara omöjligt, säger presidentfrun Melania Trump. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. I ett pressmeddelande från Vita huset uppger presidentfrun att representanter från hennes stab höra förhandlat fram en vapenvila för staden Oleshky, i södra Ukraina. – Oleshky är en krigsstad vid frontlinjen på randen till katastrof. Den kvarvarande befolkningen består främst av äldre invånare som är i akut behov av sjukvård, mediciner, mat och rent vatten, säger Melania Trump i pressmeddelandet. Vapenvilan inleds den 27 oktober och är endast tillfällig. Kirill Dmitrijev, Putins sändebud i Ukrainakriget, uppger i ett inlägg på X att Kreml bekräftar vapenvilan. Enligt sändebudet gäller vapenvilan, i motsats till Vita husets uppgifter, hela Cherson-regionen, där staden ligger. ”Ryssland välkomnar presidentfrun Melania Trumps nyckelroll i den humanitära Oleshky-operationen, säger Kremls talesperson Peskov”, skriver Dimitrijev. Frontlinjen skär genom staden som har drabbats hårt under Rysslands anfallskrig mot Ukraina. Befolkningen har minskat med 24 000 personer till knappt 2 000 under stridernas gång. Förutom mestadels äldre människor uppges även ett 50-tal barn finnas kvar, enligt Vita huset. Enligt pressmeddelandet har Melanias stab förhandlat fram villkoren för vapenvilan direkt med det ryska och ukrainska ledarskapet.
